html:
SMTO-SCH-0023 — The Agent tried to start before your requested wait was over

GUID: 495f3d60-31b1-45a8-8f0d-a6ffe49d49f7
Slug: same-run-wait-required
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • You asked the Agent to wait before doing the work, but it tried to start early. SMTO stopped that step before it ran and told the Agent to wait first.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Keep the conversation open and watch the run. The Agent normally starts the wait on its own after this. SMTO sends the Agent back to wait the amount of time you asked for.
  2. If the run stops instead, check whether any of the work already happened before you ask again. Asking again without checking could make the work happen twice.
  3. Then send a new message that states the wait clearly, for example "wait 10 minutes, then restart the web server". A clear wait time lets the Agent do the wait first and the work after.

What success looks like

  • The run shows a timed wait, and the work starts only after that time has passed.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the request quickly while it is waiting. Don't turn off the Enforce temporal routing check to get past this; it could make the Agent act at the wrong time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Temporal routing blocked a proposed action because the captured same-run time wait has not completed and the action was not a time wait.

What this means

  • A captured same_run_wait is not satisfied and the model proposes an action other than a time wait. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • A captured same_run_wait is not satisfied and the model proposes an action other than a time wait.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect wait kind/phase and the proposed tool action; independent future tasks use a different scheduling route.

How to fix it

  • temporal_routing.guard found temporal_route.kind=same_run_wait with phase other than wait_satisfied and a proposed action other than wait_for_event(kind=time). The model must call wait_for_event with the captured timing first; a deferred task for a later date belongs in the separate scheduling flow, not in this run.
  • Use the supported time wait and let it complete before beginning the requested work. A future scheduled task uses the separate scheduling flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported same-run time wait satisfies the captured timing before work begins.

What not to do

  • Do not use a rapid retry loop or replay an uncertain mutation while waiting for the stated condition.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
